group_assessment.weighting: The Chang laboratory (National Cheng Kung University, from the authors' contributions), a many-author mouse and cell paper on a synthetic peptide. Primary for the Zfra peptide, not for Wwox loss of function; WWOX enters through one heterozygous mouse and the binding of Zfra to WWOX. Tumour-curve observations are weighed above the Z-cell and 'memory' interpretation.

entries.proposition: The text gives the cure rate of Wwox+/- tumours by Zfra4-10 as 70 percent of ten mice while the Figure 5E legend gives 75 percent of ten mice; 75 percent is not a possible fraction of ten.
entries.snippet: Zfra completely cured the cancer in 50 days, and the successful rate was 70% by examining 10 mice (Figure 5E).
entries.anchor: Results, Zfra4-10 induces a memory anticancer response against many types of cancer cells in vivo, paragraph 3

entries.proposition: The paper restates, for the WWOX link, that overexpressed WWOX induces cytochrome c release and that Zfra blocks it, citing the Cell Signal paper; this is a restatement of an in vitro overexpression result, not a result here.
entries.snippet: One of the mechanisms for Zfra inhibition of cytochrome c release is that transiently overexpressed WWOX induces cytochrome c release, and that Zfra binds and blocks the function of WWOX [3].
